questions.q: What should a business do first when choosing where to be on social media?
a: Find out where its target customers already spend time online
Sign up for every major platform at once
Copy the posting habits of the biggest brands
Start with paid ads before posting anything
questions.why: Lesson 1 says each platform has its own rules, so test where your customers already are.

questions.q: What mix of posts does the summary recommend for social media?
a: Eighty percent social content and twenty percent promotion
Fifty percent social content and fifty percent promotion
Twenty percent social content and eighty percent promotion
Ninety percent promotion with occasional personal posts
questions.why: Lesson 1 recommends an 80/20 split between social content and promotional posts.

questions.q: What makes an email list worth the effort, according to the summary?
a: Valuable content that also serves the company's goals
Daily discounts sent to the largest possible list
A purchased list of contacts in your industry
Fully automated emails that never change
questions.why: Lesson 2 says email must balance serving the audience with meeting company goals.

questions.q: How does the summary suggest judging whether online efforts are working?
a: Set business goals and review the numbers every week
Count how many posts went out this month
Compare follower totals with rival companies
Ask the team whether the work feels busy
questions.why: Lesson 3 recommends weekly review of metrics tied to clear business goals.

questions.q: What should you do if one social platform is a struggle?
a: Move to another platform instead of forcing it
Post more often until the audience appears
Pay for followers to build quick momentum
Hire a team to run every platform at once
questions.why: Lesson 1 says to focus on one or two platforms and move on if one does not work.
